provenanceLimit: Curator numeric preview transcribed; curator endpoint not retrievable during browser research. Primary article independently checked for design, sampling and stated 8 h concentration. Values were not independently redigitised.

context.title: Tanaka et al. 2014 — caffeine in a CYP-probe cocktail
context.citation: Tanaka S et al. Biological and Pharmaceutical Bulletin 37 (2014), 18–25. DOI 10.1248/bpb.b13-00401; Figure 3 and Application of the Assay.
context.population: Four healthy male volunteers aged 34–41 years. Body masses were not extracted. Repeated group means at nine times are not nine independent participants.
context.administration: Oral caffeine 100 mg, losartan 50 mg, omeprazole 20 mg, dextromethorphan 30 mg and midazolam 1 mg. Requested caffeine abstinence for 72 h. Plasma LC-MS/MS; samples at 0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 6 and 8 h.
context.statistics: Group arithmetic means; digitised SEM used only as a declared descriptive error scale, not individual measurement SD.
context.assumptions: PK-DB curator CSV (Tanaka2014), digitised from Figure 3; ng/mL retained. Values and SEM transcribed at the curator precision from its indexed preview. The raw curator endpoint could not be retrieved for this release; the figure was not independently redigitised. The publication states 2480 ng/mL at 8 h; curator digitisation is 2470.59 ng/mL (~0.38% lower). No interpolation or baseline subtraction of observations. Reconstruction assumes 70 kg, 37.5 years, direct 5 h half-life, reference distribution volume and light-meal defaults, instantaneous oral input and initial central caffeine matching the observed predose mean. The predose row is marked calibration for initialisation; the eight postdose rows are reserved for evaluation. Weight, food and ingestion duration were not reported here. Other cocktail drugs and their interactions are not modelled. This is a qualified reconstruction and descriptive transportability check, not validation of individual predictions or a reason to revise the reference equations.

diagnostics.method: Residual = predicted minus observed. Standardised residuals use supplied converted SD or the declared default error scale. Censored observations contribute one-sided exceedance penalties only, not signed measurement residuals. Trend slopes/correlations are descriptive; repeated group means, sparse rows and heterogeneous errors do not support an independent-error inference.

interpretation: Descriptive discrepancies conditional on assumed weight, food, ingestion duration, priors and predose initialisation. Group means from four participants are not independent individual trajectories; coadministered probes are unmodelled. This does not isolate structural bias or establish individual predictive validity.
